title: Evidence-gated acceptance
subtitle: A capability counts only when evidence shows it wired and exercised at runtime, and the gates say what is still unproven.

stats.label: Rust tests passed by the meeting tools, kept open until their runtime gates passed
integration tests that list what they leave unproven
lines of hardening modules built, and kept apart from what guards requests

lede: AI engineering teams produce plausible claims that something works, and live tests in a real Microsoft tenant are scarce, so I set Helix a strict vocabulary. Unit tests prove a thing is implemented, a runtime trace proves it is wired, and a live session proves it works in the meeting. Every meeting action moved through those states, and nothing counted as complete until its live gate passed; the second-generation meeting tools passed every Rust test and every stage test, and I kept them open until the live gates passed. Where Microsoft's platform has no supported path, the action fails closed and says why.
quote: A mocked backend never counts as proven live.
evidence: Evidence-gated acceptance: meeting tools that passed 55 of 55 Rust tests kept open until their runtime gates passed in the meeting.
Quality engineering for AI-produced work: 47 integration tests that list what they leave unproven, with failed gates kept in the history.
Documentation audited against code: system dossiers re-documented from the code with drift tables, where the code wins any disagreement.
author: Corey James
